questions.question: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the Statements: All pages are diaries. Some diaries are books. All books are notebooks. Conclusions: I. No page is a notebook. II. All pages are notebooks. III. All diaries being notebooks is a possibility.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if
they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the
 
Statements:
All pages are diaries.
Some diaries are books.
All books are notebooks.
Conclusions:
I. No page is a notebook.
II. All pages are notebooks.
III. All diaries being notebooks is a possibility.

options.text: Both conclusion I and II follow
options.html: Both conclusion I and II follow

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and III follow

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. No page is a notebook → Does not follow (As all pages are diaries, some diaries are books and all books are notebooks. As no direct relation is given between pages and notebooks, therefore it is false.)

II. All pages are notebooks → Does not follow (As all pages are diaries, some diaries are books and all books are notebooks. So it is possible but not definite.)

III. All diaries being notebooks is a possibility → Follow (As some diaries are books and all books are notebooks. As statement restricts whole diaries from being books therefore it is possible and thus is true.)

questions.question: Six words Eat, Cry, Play, Sleep, Run and Bath are written on different faces of a dice. Three positions of this dice are shown in the figure. Find the word on the face opposite to Eat.
questions.questionHtml: Six words Eat, Cry, Play, Sleep, Run and Bath are written on different faces of a dice. Three positions of this dice are shown in the figure. Find the word on the face opposite to Eat.
questions.solution:
As Play is common on both the dices I and III, it is clear that Eat, Cry, Run, and Sleep are adjacent to it, and the remaining i.e. Bath will be opposite to it.

​

Opposite pairs:

Cry → Sleep, Eat → Run, Play → Bath

questions.question: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 342 × 18 + 79 − 45 ÷ 3 = ?
questions.questionHtml:
What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’
are interchanged?
342 × 18 + 79 − 45 ÷ 3 = ?
questions.solution:
Given equation: 342 × 18 + 79 − 45 ÷ 3 = ?

Now, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged, then:

⇒ 342 ÷ 18 - 79 + 45 × 3 = ? ⇒ 19 - 79 + 45 × 3 

= 19 - 79 + 135 ⇒ 154 - 79 = 75.
